findings.summary: The test comment says a stopped (recordedRewrite) page is refused too, but no test exercises that path. The test also never checks that a refused page is left out of the backup.
evidence: The guard at migrate_cards.go:393 runs after the switch that sets newBlock = stopped at line 388, so the recovery path is covered by the code.
The only new unit test, TestMigrateCardPages_AMemoryTypeEndingInRulesMakesARefusalAndNoWrite, uses a plain legacy page with a stored entry that matches it. No half-migrated page is built.
That test checks that the page bytes and its precedence entry are unchanged. It does not assert on m.backup.calls or on the backup contents for the refused page.
In the code a refused page never reaches plan, so the backup cannot include it. This is a gap in test pinning, not a defect.

findings.summary: The refusal uses the generic kind RefusedOther. It is identified by its reason text, and the command-line test matches that text as a substring. The text names the memory's type or revision, but only the type can currently trigger it.
evidence: rewrittenIdentity (lines 579-603) writes source as the constant memorycardSource, source_id as FormatInt(memoryID), and revision from m.revision. All are numeric or constant except kind.
Only the memory type (kind) can currently end the block early, so the 'or revision' wording in the reason is slightly misleading. It is harmless.
The refusal is appended to report.Refused, and the command-line test sees `refused c-000901:` in stderr with exit exitRegistrationConflict. It is counted and named.
Read migrate_cards.go lines 205-462 and 579-640 in the worktree. These cover shapeOf, MigrateCardPages, recordedRewrite, rewrittenIdentity and applyMigration.

The guard at line 393 runs in the single planning loop, after both the matching-entry case and the recordedRewrite case. Dry-run and --apply share that loop, so one check covers both. Refused pages never enter plan, which is all applyMigration backs up and writes.

The check is shapeOf(newBlock+body) == newBlock with shapeReadable. shapeOf calls frontmatterBlock and requires it to equal the first \n---\n split. Any identity value that ended the block early would be caught.
frontmatterBlock in address.go (lines 81-88) is unchanged. I did not diff the commit, so that the commit leaves MatchesPage unchanged is not confirmed.

Read the new unit test (migrate_cards_unreadable_test.go:134) and the command-line test (migrate_card_pages_scan_test.go:123). Both go through the public entry points, MigrateCardPages and runMigrate --apply.
Not run: the Go tests and any mutation or differential checks. Docs changes were not checked.
